claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.note: Section heading printed in the PDF is transcribed as a plain paragraph with no Markdown heading marker, so it is lost from the document outline; should be '### 7.3.2 Section Header' (siblings such as 7.2.4 / 7.2 carry headings).

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page 189 (folio IV-43) prints '7.3.2 Section Header' as a numbered clause heading on its own line, styled like 7.2.5, 7.3.1 and 7.3.3. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 7856 it is a bare paragraph '7.3.2 Section Header' with no '#' marker, while the sibling clauses of the same part carry markers: '## 7.2 REFERENCE FORMAT REPRESENTATION' (line 7776) and '### 7.2.1'-'### 7.2.4' (lines 7816-7834). So the clause is missing from the heading outline. This is a real structural defect, and the claim describes it accurately. The neighbouring 7.2.5, 7.3, 7.3.1 and 7.3.3 lines are unmarked too; this claim covers only 7.3.2.
